# remove-profanity

> Offline profanity/abuse detector for English and ten Indian languages, in
> native script and in romanized form (Hinglish, Banglish, Tanglish, …). Zero
> runtime dependencies, TypeScript types bundled, ESM.

## What it does, and does not

- DOES: detect listed profanity in Devanagari, Bengali, Gurmukhi, Gujarati,
  Odia, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam and Latin script; resolve evasions
  (leetspeak, Unicode homoglyphs, zero-width injection, letter stretching,
  interior masks like `f*ck`, spelled-out `s.h.i.*`, chunk splits `as sh o*e`);
  report severity 0-4, categories, and exact character spans; censor in
  grapheme clusters.
- DOES NOT: classify toxicity, harassment, sarcasm, or intent; detect
  languages; call any network service; learn from data. It is a dictionary
  plus a matching engine. Its output is a signal for your policy, not a
  verdict.
- KNOWN MISSES (deliberate, not bugs): mixed-script words (`मा` + `darch*d`),
  disemvowelling (`fck`), masks at a token edge (`f***`, `*uck`), two
  space-separated chunks (`fu c*`), doubled separators (`f..uc*`).

## Install

```
npm install remove-profanity
```

Requires Node >= 18. The package is ESM only (`"type": "module"`).

ESM:

```js
import { createMatcher } from 'remove-profanity';
import { hindi } from 'remove-profanity/data/hi';
```

CommonJS (dynamic import; there is no CJS build):

```js
const { createMatcher } = await import('remove-profanity');
const { hindi } = await import('remove-profanity/data/hi');
```

## MCP server — you may not need to write code at all

The package ships an MCP server as a bin, `remove-profanity-mcp`. If you are an
agent with an MCP client, calling it is usually better than writing code against
the library: no build step, and the matcher is constructed once at launch
instead of once per script run. Still zero runtime dependencies — the stdio
JSON-RPC transport is implemented directly, not via `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk`.

Client configuration:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "remove-profanity": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "-p", "remove-profanity", "remove-profanity-mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

`-p remove-profanity` is required: the bin lives inside that package rather than
in one named after itself.

Four tools, all read-only:

| Tool | Input | Output |
|---|---|---|
| `check_text` | `text`, `languages?`, `minSeverity?` | `clean`, `matchCount`, `maxSeverity`, `languages` |
| `scan_text` | same | `matches[]` (`surface`, `lemma`, `language`, `severity`, `categories`, `tier`, `casualUse`, `start`, `end`), `matchCount`, `maxSeverity`, `languages` |
| `censor_text` | same plus `mask?`, `keepFirst?` | `censored`, `matchCount`, `maxSeverity`, `languages` |
| `list_languages` | none | `languages[]` (`code`, `name`, `scripts`, `lemmaCount`), `defaultLanguages` |

There is deliberately NO tool to add a word, edit an allowlist, read a file,
spawn a process or reach the network. A word list the model can edit is a filter
the text under review can talk into switching itself off. Use the library's
`customWords` / `customAllowlist` if you need custom terms.

Which packs load: all eleven by default (~53 ms from launch to ready, of which
~19 ms is Node's own boot). Narrow with `--languages hi,en` or
`REMOVE_PROFANITY_LANGUAGES=hi,en`, and narrow per call with the `languages`
argument. Full manual, including the protocol coverage table: `docs/mcp.md`.

## Exports

From `remove-profanity`:

```ts
function createMatcher(options: MatcherOptions): Matcher;

interface Matcher {
  scan(text: string): ScanResult;
  isClean(text: string): boolean;
  censor(text: string, options?: CensorOptions): string;
}

function censorText(
  text: string,
  spans: { start: number; end: number }[],
  options?: CensorOptions,
): string;

function skeletonKey(word: string): string;
```

Exported types: `Category`, `CensorOptions`, `LanguagePack`, `LemmaEntry`,
`Matcher`, `MatcherOptions`, `MatchTier`, `ProfanityMatch`, `ScanResult`,
`Severity`.

`censorText` masks spans you supply yourself (e.g. after filtering `scan()`
results by your own rules). `skeletonKey` exposes the phonetic key used by the
skeleton tier; it is a debugging aid for pack authors, not a filter.

## Options — every field, type, and default

`MatcherOptions` (passed to `createMatcher`):

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `packs` | `LanguagePack[]` | required |
| `minSeverity` | `0 \| 1 \| 2 \| 3 \| 4` | `0` |
| `categories` | `Category[]` | undefined (all categories reported) |
| `skeletonTier` | `boolean \| 'flag'` | `true` |
| `maskedTier` | `boolean` | `true` |
| `customWords` | `string[]` | undefined (none) |
| `customAllowlist` | `string[]` | undefined (none) |

- `minSeverity` — suppress matches strictly below this value. Default `0`
  reports EVERYTHING the loaded packs list, mild insults included.
- `categories` — if set, only matches carrying at least one listed category
  are reported.
- `skeletonTier` — the high-recall phonetic tier. `true` = on, matches look
  like any other; `'flag'` = on, and the caller is expected to review rather
  than block (matches carry `tier: 'skeleton'` either way); `false` = off.
- `maskedTier` — resolve masked tokens (`f*ck`, `bh#sd*ke`) against the
  dictionary. Mask characters are `* # @ $ %`, one to three per token, never
  at a token edge.
- `customWords` — extra terms, registered as `language: 'custom'`,
  `severity: 2`, `categories: ['general']`.
- `customAllowlist` — extra phrases that must never match.

`CensorOptions` (passed to `matcher.censor` / `censorText`):

| Field | Type | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `mask` | `string` | `'*'` |
| `keepFirst` | `boolean` | `false` |

`mask` is repeated once per grapheme cluster of the match. `keepFirst` leaves
the first grapheme cluster visible.

`Severity` = `0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4` (4 = extreme slur / sexual-violence term,
3 = strong profanity, 2 = moderate insult, 1 = mild insult).

`Category` = `'slur' | 'casteist' | 'religious' | 'gendered' | 'sexual' |
'ableist' | 'violence' | 'general'`.

## What `scan()` returns

```ts
interface ScanResult {
  matches: ProfanityMatch[];
  maxSeverity: Severity | null;   // null when matches is empty, NOT 0
}

interface ProfanityMatch {
  lemma: string;        // canonical entry, native script where one exists
  surface: string;      // exact slice of the ORIGINAL text that matched
  tier: 'exact' | 'masked' | 'separated' | 'skeleton';
  language: string;     // ISO 639-1 code of the matching pack, or 'custom'
  severity: 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4;
  categories: Category[];
  start: number;        // UTF-16 code-unit index into the ORIGINAL string
  end: number;          // exclusive
  casualUse: boolean;   // term is often conversational, not abusive
}
```

Concrete example, using a benign custom word so the output is printable:

```js
const matcher = createMatcher({ packs: [english], customWords: ['heck'] });
matcher.scan('what the heck');
// {
//   matches: [{
//     lemma: 'heck', surface: 'heck', tier: 'exact', language: 'custom',
//     severity: 2, categories: ['general'], casualUse: false,
//     start: 9, end: 13
//   }],
//   maxSeverity: 2
// }
```

`start`/`end` index the string you passed in, so slicing, highlighting and
censoring against the original text are safe — all normalization happens on
internal shadow copies with offset maps.

## Per-language subpath imports

| Import | Export |
|---|---|
| `remove-profanity/data/hi` | `hindi` |
| `remove-profanity/data/en` | `english` |
| `remove-profanity/data/ta` | `tamil` |
| `remove-profanity/data/bn` | `bengali` |
| `remove-profanity/data/mr` | `marathi` |
| `remove-profanity/data/or` | `odia` |
| `remove-profanity/data/te` | `telugu` |
| `remove-profanity/data/kn` | `kannada` |
| `remove-profanity/data/ml` | `malayalam` |
| `remove-profanity/data/pa` | `punjabi` |
| `remove-profanity/data/gu` | `gujarati` |

Load only the languages the application actually needs. Each pack is
self-sufficient — it carries the romanizations it shares with other packs, so
you never need Hindi loaded to catch a borrowed word in Marathi. Measured, ten
of the eleven packs score identically alone and with all eleven loaded.

Loading everything costs two things:

1. Construction time: 33.71 ms cold for all eleven, versus a few ms for one or
   two.
2. Cross-language false positives: a word innocent in one language may be
   listed in another. Measured, Marathi has zero false positives on its own
   clean suite alone and one with all eleven loaded.

Per-CHECK cost is nearly flat past the first two packs: `en`+`hi` to all
eleven adds 212 lemmas and moves a 20,000-word check by 0%.

## Recipes

### 1. Moderate a chat message

```js
import { createMatcher } from 'remove-profanity';
import { hindi } from 'remove-profanity/data/hi';
import { english } from 'remove-profanity/data/en';

// Build ONCE at module scope. Construction is the expensive part.
const matcher = createMatcher({ packs: [hindi, english] });

export function moderate(message) {
  const { matches, maxSeverity } = matcher.scan(message);
  if (matches.length === 0) return { action: 'allow', text: message };
  if (maxSeverity >= 4) return { action: 'block', matches };
  return { action: 'censor', text: matcher.censor(message), matches };
}
```

### 2. Censor a document

```js
const clean = matcher.censor(document);                       // full masking
const soft = matcher.censor(document, { keepFirst: true });   // 'f***'
const dashed = matcher.censor(document, { mask: '-' });
```

`censor` masks per grapheme cluster, so Devanagari and other Indic matches do
not leave orphaned combining marks behind.

### 3. English only

```js
import { createMatcher } from 'remove-profanity';
import { english } from 'remove-profanity/data/en';

const matcher = createMatcher({ packs: [english] });
matcher.isClean(text);
```

### 4. Per-language matcher, chosen at request time

```js
import { createMatcher } from 'remove-profanity';
import { english } from 'remove-profanity/data/en';
import { hindi } from 'remove-profanity/data/hi';
import { tamil } from 'remove-profanity/data/ta';

// One matcher per locale, all built at startup.
const matchers = {
  en: createMatcher({ packs: [english] }),
  hi: createMatcher({ packs: [english, hindi] }),
  ta: createMatcher({ packs: [english, tamil] }),
};

export const check = (locale, text) =>
  (matchers[locale] ?? matchers.en).isClean(text);
```

### 5. Strong slurs only, everything milder allowed

```js
const matcher = createMatcher({
  packs: [hindi, english],
  minSeverity: 3,
  categories: ['slur', 'casteist', 'religious'],
});
```

### 6. Flag for human review instead of blocking

```js
const matcher = createMatcher({ packs: [hindi, english], skeletonTier: 'flag' });

for (const m of matcher.scan(text).matches) {
  if (m.tier === 'skeleton' || m.casualUse) queueForReview(m);
  else block(m);
}
```

## Common mistakes

1. **`minSeverity` defaults to `0`.** Every listed term is flagged, including
   the mildest. If the product only wants strong profanity, set
   `minSeverity: 3` explicitly. Do not assume low-severity entries are
   advisory — only `minSeverity` makes them so.
2. **Do not load all eleven packs by default.** It costs 33.71 ms of startup
   and adds cross-language false positives (a word innocent in one Indian
   language is listed in another). Load the languages the app actually needs.
3. **Build the matcher once, at module scope.** Construction is 33.71 ms cold
   and 11.50 ms warm; a check on a 10-word message is 0.003 ms. Building per
   request is the single biggest performance mistake available here.
4. **`isClean()` and `scan()` cost the same on clean text.** `isClean()` exits
   early only when something matches. Choose by what you need back, not for
   speed.
5. **`maxSeverity` is `null`, not `0`, when the text is clean.** Test
   `matches.length` or call `isClean()`; `maxSeverity === 0` is a real
   severity level.
6. **Masks at a token edge are not detected.** `f***`, `*uck`, `fuc*` are
   deliberate misses (markdown italics and footnote asterisks would collide).
   Interior masks — `f*ck`, `b***h` — are detected. Do not write a test that
   expects `f***` to be caught.
7. **`categories` filters, it does not rank.** A match is reported if it
   carries ANY listed category.
8. **`casualUse: true` annotates; it does not suppress.** Terms like `sa*la`
   and the literal "pig" sense of `su*r` still appear in `matches`. Filter on
   the flag yourself if you want lighter handling.
9. **Spans index the original string.** Do not re-derive offsets from a
   lowercased or normalized copy; `start`/`end` already point at the input.
10. **The package is ESM.** `require('remove-profanity')` fails; use
    `await import(...)` from CommonJS.
11. **Adding a term is `customWords`, not editing the pack.** Terms added that
    way get `severity: 2` and `categories: ['general']`; if you need a
    different severity, filter on `language === 'custom'` yourself.
12. **It does not detect the input language.** Pick packs from your own locale
    signal.

## Performance reference

Median of 7 trials, node v22.22.3 on darwin/arm64, all eleven packs loaded.
Full tables and methodology: `docs/benchmarks.md`, `benchmark/results.txt`.

| Operation | Cost |
|---|---|
| `isClean()` on a 10-word message | 0.003 ms |
| `isClean()` on a 1,000-word document | 0.102 ms |
| `isClean()` on a 20,000-word ASCII document | 1.987 ms |
| `isClean()` on 20,000 words of Devanagari | 6.359 ms |
| `scan()` on a 20,000-word ASCII document | 1.910 ms |
| `createMatcher` with 11 packs, cold | 33.71 ms |
| `createMatcher` with 11 packs, warm rebuild | 11.50 ms |

## Accuracy reference

Against a 97-axis evasion battery owned and published by this project:

- English evasion: 81 of 88 caught (92%). Second-best is 61 of 88.
- All eleven languages: 801 of 952 evasion cases; 151 missed.
- False positives: 3 of 486 clean cases.
- Dictionary sweep: 464 hits over 1,771,208 English word forms, of which 46
  are real headwords.
- Speed: second of six on a 20,000-word Latin document. `leo-profanity` is 3x
  faster and catches 18 of the 88 evasion cases.
